questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in staying and studying in Japan for a period

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was ok easy to find, but there was just many procedures one had to complete

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was orientation for new students and an international office where we could ask questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, I just applied for the housing that the school offered

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If it is accommodation offered by the university, it will still be close to campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of procedures. I think they did a good job trying tell us what to do, including a pre-arrival, arrival, and departure guidebook, but I wish there was less procedures and bureacracy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had a meeting where they told us about the procedures we had to complete, and gave us a guidebook about it. That is things like insurances, memberships for coop (so one can buy food and books at campus), bicycle registration, national residency card registration, health insurance, bank account etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were very helpful at the international office. And there was also some Japanese students who tried to assist us.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to follow the guidelines and remember to sort stuff at the required deadlines

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the courses were a bit too small (4 ects each) and superficial for my taste. I also didn't like the that attendance was registered and there was so many small (but superficial) assignments. It seemed a bit more like high school sometimes. But I did have some courses and teachers that I liked, and I also did learn some interesting things.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As written above, I think the level was a bit low. There was a lot of homework and attendance were taken, but the substance was not often that deep, which is a shame

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar style, but a bit more seminar style generally.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Lecture for Humanities (Japanese Early Poetry, and Japanese traditional culture)
Race and Ethnicity in the Modern World
Japanese Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Japanese Early Poetry and Race and Ethnicity in the Modern World

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a whole list of social clubs that one could join

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did kintsugi, that was interesting and fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel, there is so much to see!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's very different. But I also enjoyed this aspect, even when at times it was difficult

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That most people don't speak English

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of the people and the rich traditions of crafts, poetry, arts etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a lot of bureaucracy and procedures in the beginning and end, more homework and attendance requirements than in DK, but also a fascinating country, culture, food and kind people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Spending time in a culture that is so different from Denmark

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier -- most people don't speak English

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
